Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and sorry for the operational friction. Short answers up front:

1) Preferred: please pay in the invoice currency (USD). That avoids FX spread and simplifies reconciliation.
2) If you must pay in EUR, we can accept it, but the receiving bank will convert and any intermediary charges or FX spread will be deducted by the banks (not Redwood).
3) To avoid intermediary fees for EUR payments, use our EU SEPA account (details below). For USD wires to our US account, some banks route via an intermediary (often Deutsche Bank or Citibank in Europe) — that can trigger an intermediary fee.

Our recommended routing options:

- Option A (no intermediary fees for EUR): SEPA transfer to Redwood Inference Ltd (EUR account) — see attached PDF with full SEPA details.
  Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd
  IBAN: IE29SBIN90012345678901
  BIC/SWIFT: SBINIE2D
  Bank: SBI Europe (Dublin Branch)

- Option B (USD wire to US HQ) — may incur intermediary bank fees depending on your bank
  Beneficiary: Redwood Inference, Inc.
  Bank: Wells Fargo Bank NA
  ABA/ACH (Routing): 121000248
  SWIFT: WFBIUS6S
  Account: 9876543210
  Note: Some EU banks will route USD through an intermediary like Deutsche Bank AG (DEUTDEFF) — if your bank provides an option to credit our account via a correspondent bank to avoid extra charges, please confirm with them.

If you want us to absorb a single intermediary fee for a one-off and speed the payment, we can discuss a credit, but that needs approval from finance (CC'd).

I've attached a short SEPA details PDF for your AP team. Let me know which route you'd like to use and we can confirm invoice clearing ETA.

Hi Olivia / Rafael — quick finance clarification:

- Standard policy: we invoice in the agreed contract currency. If the payer initiates payment in a different currency, any bank fees and FX spread are deducted by the banks and are not covered by Redwood unless pre-agreed.
- For EU customers with VAT-registered entities that want invoices in EUR, we can issue future invoices in EUR if contract amendment is executed. For this one-off invoice (12345) we're sticking to USD as issued.

On intermediary fees: if Acme would like Redwood to cover a single intermediary fee to unblock payment, we can approve reimbursement up to EUR 25. Rafael — if Acme routes via USD to the US account and the bank charges an intermediary > EUR 25, they will need to either: (a) re-send with cover charges OUR (SHA) or (b) send via SEPA to our Irish entity.

Please confirm preferred routing and whether Acme can reissue in SEPA.
